# Tree view syntax

<!-- Generated by tools/gen-grammar from packages/diagram-treeview/grammar/treeview.ebnf. Do not edit: run `pnpm gen:grammar`. -->

TreeView syntax (R-PARSE-9, D54): the normative grammar of `treeView-beta` diagrams.

The hand-written parser in `src/parser/` implements it; `tools/gen-grammar` builds a reference
parser, a sentence generator, highlighters and the syntax reference page from it. mermaid@12
decides what is valid, this file is fixed to match, and the parser must match this file
(DESIGN §4.4). mermaid@12 parsed treeView with Langium (`treeView.langium` in
`@mermaid-js/parser`, which does not import `common.langium`); the rules below are its token
rules, in its order, and its grammar.

**Lexer input.** The lexer reads the diagram body as mermaid@12 handed it to its lexer: front
matter and `%%{…}%%` directives removed; CRLF and CR read as LF; `="x"` inside an HTML tag read
as `='x'`; `%%` comment lines removed and leading blanks trimmed; `#name;` / `#123;` entities
read as opaque text; a line break appended; and then, when a line is exactly `treeView-beta`
(blanks around it aside) and a later line draws a tree with `├──`, `└──` and `│` (or `┣━━`,
`┗━━`, `┃`), each such line rewritten to four spaces per level and its name (tabs read as four
spaces, `│`-only lines dropped). Keywords are case-sensitive.

**Line breaks are skipped.** Nothing ends a node: two nodes may share a line (`"a" b`), an
annotation may sit on the next line, and a node's indent is the run of blanks right before its
name, wherever it is, so a blank at the end of a line indents the node on the next line, and a
second blank run before an indented node is an error. The first rule that matches wins, except
that `treeView-beta` gives way to a longer name.

## Grammar

EBNF: `[ x ]` is optional, `{ x }` repeats zero or more times, `x+` one or more times, `|` separates alternatives. Upper-case names and `subgraph`, `end`, `acc_…`, `direction_…` are tokens (see below). A rule marked `@Type` builds an AST node of that type.

```ebnf
treeView = Header { text } { Node } EOF ;
```

`treeView-beta`: starts a tree view.

```ebnf
Header @Header = TREEVIEW_BETA ;
```

```ebnf
text = Title
     | AccTitle
     | AccDescr ;
```

A node: its indent, its name, then its annotations in any order. Nodes nest by indent: a
node goes under the nearest node before it with a smaller indent, or at the top.

```ebnf
Node @Node = [ INDENTATION ] ( QUOTED_NAME | BARE_NAME ) { CLASS_ANNOTATION | ICON_ANNOTATION | DESC_ANNOTATION } ;
```

`title Files`: the title of the diagram (the last one wins).

```ebnf
Title @Title = TITLE ;
```

`accTitle: …`: the accessible title.

```ebnf
AccTitle @AccTitle = ACC_TITLE ;
```

`accDescr: …` or `accDescr { … }`: the accessible description.

```ebnf
AccDescr @AccDescr = ACC_DESCR ;
```

## Tokens

The lexer works in modes (`INITIAL` and the ones below). In each mode it tries the rules in this order and takes the first that matches; a rule may push a mode or pop back to the previous one. Rules without a token emit nothing.

Modes: `INITIAL`.

| Modes | Token | Pattern | Action | Doc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| INITIAL | TREEVIEW_BETA | `treeView-beta(?=[\n\r]\|$\|[\t ]+(?::::[\t ]*[A-Z_a-z]\|icon\(\|##))` |  | `treeView-beta`: starts a tree view. Nothing may follow it on its line. |
| INITIAL | ACC_DESCR | `[\t ]*accDescr[\t ]*:(?:[^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[^\n\r]*)` |  | `accDescr: …` (the rest of the line) or `accDescr { … }` (over lines, to `}`): the accessible description of the diagram, before the first node. mermaid@12's one rule, as two tried in order; the block's `[\s\S]*?\}` is its `[^}]*\}`, written so that line-based highlighters read the block as one span. |
| INITIAL | ACC_DESCR | `[\t ]*accDescr\s*\{[\s\S]*?\}` |  |  |
| INITIAL | ACC_TITLE | `[\t ]*accTitle[\t ]*:(?:[^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[^\n\r]*)` |  | `accTitle: …`: the accessible title of the diagram, the rest of the line, before the first node. |
| INITIAL | TITLE | `[\t ]*title(?:[\t ][^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[\t ][^\n\r]*\|)` |  | `title …`: the title of the diagram (kept, not drawn), the rest of the line, before the first node. `title` alone is an empty title, so a first node `title.txt` is read as `title` and a node `.txt`: write it in quotes. |
| INITIAL | CLASS_ANNOTATION | `[\t ]+:::[\t ]*[A-Z_a-z][\w-]*` |  | ` :::name`: the class of the node before it (`highlight` draws a highlighted row). The last one written wins. |
| INITIAL | ICON_ANNOTATION | `[\t ]+icon\([\w-]*(?::[\w-]+)?\)` |  | ` icon(name)` or ` icon(pack:name)`: the icon of the node before it; `icon(none)` and `icon()` draw none. The last one written wins. |
| INITIAL | DESC_ANNOTATION | `[\t ]+##[^\n\r]*` |  | ` ## text`: the description of the node before it, the rest of the line. The last one written wins. |
| INITIAL | INDENTATION | `[\t ]+` |  | A run of blanks: the indent of the node whose name follows it; a tab counts 1. |
| INITIAL | QUOTED_NAME | `"[^"]*"\|'[^']*'` |  | `"…"` or `'…'`: a name with no escapes; it may span lines. A trailing `/` makes a directory. |
| INITIAL | COMMENT | `%%[^\n]*` |  | `%%` to the end of the line, after other text: a comment. |
| INITIAL | — | `\n` |  |  |
| INITIAL | BARE_NAME | `(?!:::\|icon\(\|##)[^\t\n\r "'](?:(?![\t ]+:::[\t ]*[A-Z_a-z]\|[\t ]+icon\(\|[\t …` |  | A name: anything to the end of the line or to a blank run before ` :::`, ` icon(` or ` ##`; its trailing blanks are cut and inner runs kept (`My Documents/`). A trailing `/` makes a directory. It cannot start with a blank, a quote, `:::`, `icon(` or `##`. |
| INITIAL | EOF | `$` |  | The end of the text. |

Removed before lexing (highlighted only):

- COMMENT: `^[^\S\n]*%%(?!\{)[^\n]+`
- DIRECTIVE: `[^\S\n]*%%\{[\s\S]*?\}%%`
